title: Extension of coefficients
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$. For a scheme $T$, use the small pro-étale site and the ordinary derived categories of sheaves of modules of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For a finite commutative ring $R$, write $R_T$ for its constant sheaf of rings [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Write $\Dctf(T_{\mathrm{proét}},R)$ for the full subcategory whose objects have bounded constructible cohomology, with constructibility as in [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf], and finite Tor amplitude as in [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude].

Let $A\to B$ be a map of finite commutative rings, each killed by a power of
$\ell$, and let $T$ be a scheme. For $K\in\Dctf(T_{\mathrm{proét}},A)$ we write

$$
K_B=K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_T}B_T\in\Dctf(T_{\mathrm{proét}},B),
$$

and for a morphism $u:K\to L$ we write
$u_B=u\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_T}\mathrm{id}_{B_T}$; this is a functor
$\Dctf(T_{\mathrm{proét}},A)\to\Dctf(T_{\mathrm{proét}},B)$. For a further map
$B\to C$ to a finite commutative ring $C$ killed by a power of $\ell$, associativity of the tensor product gives $(K_B)_C\simeq K_C$,
compatibly with morphisms.

Precisely, $(-)_B$ is the restriction to these full subcategories of the derived change-of-rings functor for $A_T\to B_T$ in [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], with the $B_T$-action on the tensor factor $B_T$. This restriction is well-defined by clause 2 of [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor]. For $A\to B\to C$ the displayed comparison is the natural associativity isomorphism of clause 4 of [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor].

For compatibility with the unit's coefficient convention, give each finite ring $R$ the discrete topology and use the condensed ring $\underline R$ of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], together with the pullback from the point [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point] and the internal/sectionwise module equivalence [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. Use the canonical ring identification $p_T^*\underline R\cong R_T$. Under these identifications, the displayed associativity isomorphism is the finite-discrete instance of clause 3 of [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback], while the restriction to the finite-Tor constructible subcategories is supplied by [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor].

proof.text: For the coefficient convention, a continuous map from a profinite set $S$ to a finite discrete ring $R$ has a finite clopen fibre partition. On this covering its restrictions are constant, so the sheaf $S\mapsto C(S,R)$ of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] is the sheafification of the constant presheaf $R$, as in [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Present the additive group of $R$ as a cokernel of a map between free abelian groups. The tensor unit is the constant abelian sheaf $\mathbf Z$ by [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. The strong monoidal left adjoint $p_T^*$ of [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point] preserves sums, cokernels, and the tensor unit, so it takes this constant presentation to the constant presentation of $R_T$. This identifies $p_T^*\underline R$ with $R_T$, naturally in $R$; multiplication and unit agree since the strong monoidal structure preserves their maps between these constant presentations.

source.place: Final compatibility paragraph: finite-discrete condensed coefficient convention and canonical identification p_T^* underline R ≅ R_T (the coefficient presentation and strong-monoidal comparison).

proof.text: The equivalence [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] leaves underlying abelian sheaves and section maps unchanged. Relative tensor products on the two sides represent the same balanced bilinear sheaf maps, so they agree canonically. Apply this equivalence termwise to complexes: cohomology, acyclicity, and the K-flat condition of [def-pc-kflat-complex] are unchanged. Consequently the derived coefficient tensors and their associativity maps agree under this equivalence, rather than merely agreeing after forgetting the coefficient actions. The small site and coefficient universe are chosen as in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. The strong monoidal sheafification of [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor] supplies the equivalence's monoidal-localization hypothesis: if $a(f)$ is invertible, then $a(f\otimes1)=a(f)\otimes1$ is invertible.

source.place: Final compatibility paragraph: internal/sectionwise module equivalence and comparison of derived coefficient tensors under the chosen coefficient categories.

proof.text: For $A_T\to B_T$, [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] supplies the ambient derived functor, with its $B_T$ action on the right factor. Clause 2 of [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor] supplies its restriction to the stated constructible finite-Tor subcategories. Clause 4 supplies the natural comparison $(K_B)_C\cong K_C$, including $\alpha_L\circ(u_B)_C=u_C\circ\alpha_K$. Under the coefficient identifications of steps 1 and 2, clause 3 of [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback] is this ambient associator: both are induced on a K-flat representative by $((x\otimes b)\otimes c)\mapsto x\otimes\varphi(b)c$, for the given map $\varphi:B\to C$.

source.place: Definition statement: restriction to Dctf and associativity for A→B→C; together with the cited det-sp-scalar-extension-functor clauses and finite-discrete instance of det-prop-scalar-six-pullback.

proof_origin.place: Coefficient convention and well-definedness of the displayed restriction and associativity
